title: Cluster identity across topic-model runs (new, merged, split)
description:
## Context
Topic-model cluster ids (BERTopic) reset on every run, so a front end cannot say "cluster 41 is new" or "cluster 17 is growing". Add a matching step that links the clusters of a run to the clusters of the previous run by document overlap (for example Jaccard on member item ids), assigns a stable cluster uid, and reports lifecycle events: new, continued, merged, split, gone.

Consumers: Papyrus initiative PPY-428252 (emerging-cluster callouts); the desk names an accepted cluster through the existing steering-proposal flow, so Biblicus only supplies identity and statistics. Parent epic: blbs-d380cb. Depends on the weekly bins story under the same epic for the growing/cooling statistic.

Known risk: BERTopic needs hundreds of documents for stable clusters; record the minimum corpus size observed.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Stable cluster identity across runs
  Scenario: A cluster continues
    Given run A produced a cluster with items {1..20}
    And run B produced a cluster with items {2..21}
    When I match run B to run A with an overlap threshold of 0.5
    Then the run B cluster keeps the stable uid of the run A cluster
    And its event is "continued"

  Scenario: A new cluster
    Given run B has a cluster that overlaps no run A cluster above the threshold
    Then it receives a new stable uid and the event "new"

  Scenario: Merge and split
    Given two run A clusters each overlap one run B cluster above the threshold
    Then the run B cluster is reported as "merged" with both predecessor uids
    And the reverse situation is reported as "split" with the successor uids

  Scenario: Deterministic
    When the same two runs are matched twice
    Then the assigned uids and events are identical
```

## Notes
Output carries uid, event, predecessor uids, member item count, top terms and first-seen date. Labels such as growing or cooling are a front-end rule applied only after four or more weeks of series data.
